#### Schemes in India

- Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (Public works, national). Run by: Ministry of Rural Development and state governments. Who is eligible: Rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. What it gives: 125 days of wage employment per financial year; wage rates vary. How it is delivered: Work on demand; wages through bank or post-office accounts. Documents: Existing job cards remain valid; the complete new application checklist was not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Published rule: weekly payment or within fifteen days of muster-roll closure; actual receipt times not verified. Why it matters in heat: Could replace some lost rural earnings, depending on work availability, safe conditions and payment timing. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Historic Commencement of Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act Across Rural India from July 1st 2026 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2259703&lang=1&reg=1

- Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: People in below-poverty-line households aged 60 or above under continuing central rules. What it gives: Central assistance: Rs.200 monthly at ages 60-79; Rs.500 at 80 or above. State additions vary. How it is delivered: State pension systems. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Regular income could help meet seasonal household costs. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Widows in below-poverty-line households aged 40 or above under continuing central rules. What it gives: Central assistance: Rs.300 monthly at ages 40-79; Rs.500 at 80 or above. State additions vary. How it is delivered: State pension systems. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Regular income could cushion seasonal earnings pressure. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: October approval expands eligibility to 40% benchmark disability and removes the minimum age; operational commencement not verified. What it gives: Approved central rates: Rs.375 monthly at ages 0-79 and Rs.625 at 80 or above. How it is delivered: State pension systems; transition guidelines pending in the announcement. Documents: Revised operational checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could support recurring costs for households including people with disabilities. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana (Cash, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Surviving household head of a below-poverty-line family after the death of its primary breadwinner aged 18-59. What it gives: Rs.20,000 under continuing central rules. How it is delivered: State-administered, demand-based assistance. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could assist an eligible family following a breadwinner's death; heat-specific receipt not verified. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- National Food Security Act foodgrain entitlement under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (Food, national). Run by: Department of Food and Public Distribution and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household beneficiaries identified by states/UTs; Maharashtra rules checked. What it gives: 35 kg per Antyodaya household monthly; 5 kg per Priority Household person monthly. Free foodgrains continue through 31 December 2028. How it is delivered: Public Distribution System. Documents: State ration-card enrolment requirements vary; complete current checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; household receipt dates unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could preserve food consumption when earnings fall; no automatic heat-related increase verified. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Maharashtra Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Department: National Food Security Act, 2013 https://s3e21e4e58ad9ab56e8a4634046da90113.s3waas.gov.in/national-food-security-act-2013/; Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars

- Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Ministry of Labour and Employment. Who is eligible: Eligible unorganised workers entering at ages 18-40, subject to income and other pension or insurance exclusions. What it gives: Rs.3,000 monthly from age 60; contributory rather than immediate income support. How it is delivered: Common Service Centres or Maandhan portal; contributions through auto-debit. Documents: Aadhaar, savings or Jan-Dhan account details with IFSC, and mobile number. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Pension starts at age 60; not a current-season payment for new entrants. Why it matters in heat: Relevant to future old-age income rather than current heat-related earnings losses. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment: Schemes https://eshram.gov.in/Schemes; Ministry of Labour and Employment, 2025: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/2e7e01b90e6358cb82f396615fc87a94.pdf

- Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (Insurance, national). Run by: Government-supported life insurance through participating banks and insurers. Who is eligible: Eligible account holders entering at ages 18-50 with consent for premium auto-debit. What it gives: Rs.2 lakh on death from any cause; annual premium Rs.436. How it is delivered: Bank-linked insurance claim. Documents: Account and enrolment consent; complete claim checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual claim-to-payment time unknown. Why it matters in heat: Death cover could help eligible surviving households; not earnings replacement during non-fatal illness. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment: Schemes https://eshram.gov.in/Schemes

- National Health Mission Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Service Initiatives (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Patients using participating public health facilities. What it gives: Specified essential medicines and diagnostic services free of cost; no household cash amount. How it is delivered: Public facilities, with packages differing by facility level. Documents: No uniform household application checklist verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Care-linked provision; actual availability and waiting time unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could reduce treatment costs, including outside hospital insurance; heat-specific availability not measured in the source. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2026: Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2292343&lang=2&reg=48

- Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Insurance, national). Run by: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, participating states and insurers. Who is eligible: Eligible farmers with insured crops in notified areas, including tenants and sharecroppers meeting state documentation conditions. What it gives: Claims depend on insured loss and sum insured. Maximum farmer premiums: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi foodgrain/oilseed crops, 5% commercial/horticultural crops. How it is delivered: Implementing insurers and enrolment channels. Documents: Insurable interest and state-defined land, tenure or sowing evidence; application and premium within deadlines. Does not follow people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual claim timing not verified. Why it matters in heat: Some heat-related crop losses could enter insured yield loss; universal farm-level heat trigger not verified. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Press Information Bureau, 2026: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2304549&lang=1&reg=48

- Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (Credit, national). Run by: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through lending institutions. Who is eligible: Eligible short-term agricultural borrowers, including specified allied activities. What it gives: 2026-27 budget note: loans up to ₹3 lakh at 7% yearly, with an additional 3% benefit for prompt repayment. How it is delivered: Concessional agricultural lending. Documents: Lender-specific checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Sanction and disbursement times unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could provide seasonal liquidity; repayable borrowing, not a heat-loss grant. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of India, 2026: Notes on Demands for Grants, 2026-2027 https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe1.pdf

- Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board benefits (Workers' welfare fund, state). Run by: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. Who is eligible: Registered workers meeting Board age, work-history and contribution conditions. What it gives: Medical and other assistance. Medical payment wording is difficult to interpret, so no reliable payable amount is reproduced. How it is delivered: Applications through area Labour Inspector. Documents: Registration: photograph, age proof, employer certificate of 90 days' construction work. Medical claims list hospital records and subscription evidence. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Unknown. Why it matters in heat: Medical assistance could help qualifying workers; heat-specific approvals and payments not verified. Status: Status unclear, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Not yet confirmed. Sources: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Frequently Asked Questions https://megbocwwb.gov.in/faqs; Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Schemes https://megbocwwb.gov.in/schemes

#### Steps of access in India (findings come from different studies of different people; they are not one funnel)

- Aware: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?

- Eligible: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?

- Documented: India, 31 October 2025: 68,14,95,972 beneficiaries completed e-KYC, stated as 85.6%. (Existing NFSA beneficiaries; limit: e-KYC is neither receipt nor every documentation requirement.; sources: Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars)

- Applied: December 2025 parliamentary reply: the Department does not maintain the pendency list. (Households awaiting a card or addition of members; limit: Describes the central record; state records may exist.; sources: Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars)

- Enrolled: India, NFHS-5, 2019-21: 41.0% had any usual member covered by a health insurance or financing scheme. (Households across health insurance and financing schemes; limit: Self-reported household coverage; not a PM-JAY enrolment rate or evidence of care received.; sources: International Institute for Population Sciences and ICF, 2022: National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 2019-21: India https://assets.exemplars.health/fd9a20fb-4386-00b3-39a1-1737868b44b7/d4b76902-0381-4d15-9661-9b2e06b58682/10%20National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%205%2020192021.pdf)

- Received: India, as of 30 June 2026: 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions authorised. (Beneficiaries accessing care outside their home state; limit: Authorisations are a proxy, not unique people or verified completed care; no heat-specific costs measured.; sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2026: Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY) https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290627&lang=1&reg=22)
- Received: India, 1 April to 2 December 2025: women accounted for 56.73% of person-days. (Women in historical MGNREGA; limit: Work participation proxy, not wage receipt or eligible-women coverage.; sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1)

- Adequate: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs?

- On time: India, 1 April to 2 December 2025: 95.31% of fund transfer orders generated within 8 days. (Historical MGNREGA workers; limit: Administrative stage, not bank receipt; predates July 2026 transition.; sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1)

#### Where no public system responds in India (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Income lost while resting: no national automatic heat-triggered informal-worker wage replacement verified. Delhi evidence records earnings losses. (Sources: Das and Somanathan, 2024: Heat causes large earnings losses for informal-sector workers in India https://heathealth.info/wp-content/uploads/Das_2024_Environ._Res._Lett._19_124019.pdf)

- Farm losses outside insurance conditions: PMFBY depends on notification, enrolment and covered risks. (Sources: Press Information Bureau, 2026: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2304549&lang=1&reg=48)

- Current shocks for new pension entrants: PM-SYM pays from age 60. (Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment, 2025: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/2e7e01b90e6358cb82f396615fc87a94.pdf)

- Debt and asset sales: no verified evaluation links public-system receipt to reductions in these heat outcomes.

- Anticipatory payments: no current public heat-forecast-triggered cash entitlement with verified rules and receipt established.

- Construction workers outside registration: checked Meghalaya benefits depend on the Board's qualifying route. (Sources: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Frequently Asked Questions https://megbocwwb.gov.in/faqs; Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Schemes https://megbocwwb.gov.in/schemes)

#### Open questions for India (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- At which access step do heat-exposed informal-worker households lose the most potential support? What is known: Separate administrative stocks and a small commissioned facilitation assessment; no complete representative ladder. A study that could answer it: Voluntary repeated survey before, during and after a hot season, publishing only aggregate group and step results. (About 1,500 households across six districts; final size depends on detectable differences.)

- Does receiving an existing transfer before peak heat improve coping compared with later receipt? What is known: Entitlements and heat earnings-loss evidence; little verified payment-timing evidence. A study that could answer it: Evaluate an authorised timing change with aggregate earnings, care costs and borrowing outcomes. (About 2,000 households across 40-60 clusters, subject to power analysis.)

- How much of household heat-illness cost is met through PM-JAY and free public care? What is known: Hospital-cover rules and service policies; no verified heat-specific cost pathway. A study that could answer it: Consent-based care-cost study across public and empanelled facilities, publishing aggregate results. (About 600 episodes across 12 facilities in one season.)

- Does assisted scheme navigation improve timely receipt during a hot season? What is known: Delivery models and commissioned assessment; no verified heat-specific causal estimate. A study that could answer it: Phased rollout of additional support against existing services, measuring receipt and timing; providers on equal terms. (About 60 communities and 1,800 households; subject to power analysis.)

- Can public works cushion heat income loss while reducing exposure? What is known: Historical learning protection evidence; no verified 2026-framework heat evaluation. A study that could answer it: Evaluate adjusted hours, rest and water provision alongside work access and wage arrival. (About 50 worksites across four districts in one hot season.)

- [Unmeasured: Adequate] Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs? What is known: Documents, applications, enrolment, receipt and payment timing are measured for some schemes, such as fund transfer orders for rural work. No source checked measures whether support is adequate in a hot season. A study that could answer it: Compare the support received with heat-season losses in the same households, in a hot month and a cooler one. (Illustrative: about 600 households in three districts)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible] How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify? What is known: Later steps are measured for some schemes; awareness and eligibility are not, in the sources checked. A study that could answer it: Pair a short awareness survey with an eligibility screen for the same workers, at worksites and markets. (Illustrative: about 800 workers in two cities)

### Indonesia (research as of 6 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- KNOWN heat evidence: insured primary-care visits increased on hotter days, including diabetes and cardiovascular visits. That study does not estimate how much insurance reduced household heat losses. (Sources: Fritz, 2022: Temperature and non-communicable diseases: Evidence from Indonesia's primary health care system https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hec.4590)

- KNOWN contextual evidence: PKH improved some child outcomes but did not increase several household economic outcomes in its historic evaluation. No heat-specific PKH causal effect was verified. (Sources: J-PAL: The Medium-Term Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Health and Education in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/medium-term-impact-conditional-cash-transfers-health-and-education-indonesia; Cahyadi et al., 2020: Cumulative Impacts of Conditional Cash Transfer Programs: Experimental Evidence from Indonesia https://swlb1.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pol.20190245)

- INFERRED map design: open climate and modelled population grids can be aggregated to a documented older province geography. Public source metadata reveals a boundary-vintage issue, so current province coverage tables are not silently joined. [Ie, Iw, Ib]

#### Schemes in Indonesia

- Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja: Bukan Penerima Upah (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Registered and contributing non-wage workers. What it gives: Medically necessary work-injury care and temporary incapacity compensation. How it is delivered: BPJS claim route; registration assistance listed in section E. Documents: NIK or KTP and email for registration; claim documents need a separate check. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Work attribution and acceptance of heat-related claims were not verified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Kematian: Bukan Penerima Upah (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Active contributors and qualifying survivors under programme conditions. What it gives: Death grant Rp20.000.000, periodic grant Rp12.000.000 and funeral Rp10.000.000. How it is delivered: Survivor claim through BPJS. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: survivor support could cushion a death-related shock; work and non-work pathways differ. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Hari Tua: Bukan Penerima Upah (Pension, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Contributors meeting withdrawal conditions. What it gives: Accumulated contributions plus investment returns; no fixed universal pension. How it is delivered: BPJS withdrawal process. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Savings are distinct from an immediate heat-triggered grant. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja and Jaminan Kematian: Jasa Konstruksi (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Covered construction-project workers. What it gives: JKK treatment and temporary incapacity pay: 100% for the first and second six-month periods, then 50%. How it is delivered: Project and BPJS arrangements. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: A relevant outdoor-worker route, with heat-specific paid-claim evidence unverified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Jaminan Keselamatan Kerja untuk Jasa Konstruksi (Jakon) https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jasa-konstruksi.html

- Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan / Ministry of Manpower. Who is eligible: Qualifying wage workers with employment termination and contribution history. What it gives: 60% of reported wage for up to six months; wage ceiling Rp. 5.000.000,00. How it is delivered: Monthly claims and labour-market services. Documents: Termination evidence and active job-search commitment; other conditions apply. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly benefit; actual processing distribution unknown. Why it matters in heat: Termination protection does not automatically replace income for a temporary hot day. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Cek Informasi Detail Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jaminan-kehilangan-pekerjaan.html

- Bantuan Subsidi Upah 2026 (Cash, national). Run by: Ministry of Manpower. Who is eligible: Qualifying citizens active as wage-earner BPJS members through August 2026; wage and other tests apply. What it gives: Not confirmed in the source we checked; see the source. How it is delivered: BPJS-sourced selection; current page awaits further recipient-check details. Documents: NIK and administrative employment/wage records; applicant process not fully announced. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: General purchasing-power support; no heat forecast trigger verified. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Manpower, 2026: Bantuan Subsidi Upah 2026 https://bsu.kemnaker.go.id/

- Kredit Usaha Rakyat: BRI offer (Credit, national). Run by: Government credit programme / Bank Rakyat Indonesia. Who is eligible: Productive viable enterprises meeting lender tests. What it gives: Super-micro up to Rp10 million at 3%; micro above Rp10 million to Rp100 million, starting at 6% yearly. How it is delivered: Participating lender; BRI terms checked. Documents: BRI 2026 offer lists NIB and NPWP; additional lender documents apply. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: working capital can help livelihoods, while the full loan remains repayable. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Bank Rakyat Indonesia, 2026: Kredit Usaha Rakyat (KUR) https://bri.co.id/web/guest/promo-detail/900

- Enrolled: Evaluation of 5,996 households: registration assistance increased enrolment by 3.5 percentage points. (Non-poor informal-worker households in Bandung and Medan; limit: Historical randomised offer, not current national access; page narrative describes 2015-2018.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)
- Enrolled: Full subsidy increased enrolment by 18.6 percentage points from a comparison mean of 7.8 percent. (Same historical evaluation population; limit: Subsidy experiment; not a 2026 policy coverage estimate.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)
- Enrolled: Additional information had no measured effect on enrolment. (Same historical evaluation population; limit: Specific information treatments and historical urban sample; not proof that all awareness work has no effect.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)

- Received: Government report, 7 August 2026: more than 7 million families had been paid in quarter III. (Programme families; limit: Interim national administrative report; no eligible-family denominator or heat subgroup.; sources: Ministry of State Secretariat, 2026: Pastikan Tepat Sasaran, Pemerintah Salurkan Bansos kepada Lebih dari 18 Juta KPM https://www.setneg.go.id/baca/index/pastikan_tepat_sasaran_pemerintah_salurkan_bansos_kepada_lebih_dari_18_juta_kpm)

#### Where no public system responds in Indonesia (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Informal heat work stoppages: JKK concerns qualifying work injury and JKP concerns qualifying termination; neither opened rule establishes general pay for every lost hot day. (Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html; BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Cek Informasi Detail Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jaminan-kehilangan-pekerjaan.html)

- Heat debt, asset sales and mortality: no evaluated public heat-transfer effect was opened. Non-heat PKH null findings are not heat null findings. (Sources: J-PAL: The Medium-Term Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Health and Education in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/medium-term-impact-conditional-cash-transfers-health-and-education-indonesia; Cahyadi et al., 2020: Cumulative Impacts of Conditional Cash Transfer Programs: Experimental Evidence from Indonesia https://swlb1.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pol.20190245)

#### Open questions for Indonesia (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- What share of diagnosed work-related heat claims reach benefit payment? What is known: JKK benefits exist; heat-specific acceptance and delay were not verified. [I5, I6] A study that could answer it: Prospective multi-site claims pathway study, publishing aggregate submitted, accepted and paid counts and time intervals. (Illustrative: several provinces over two hot seasons; sample based on case volume.)

- Does contribution support keep informal workers insured through the hot season? What is known: A registration experiment and a new contribution-saving route exist. [I16, I9] A study that could answer it: Cluster randomisation of assisted contribution-saving access, measuring active coverage, care costs and retention in aggregate. (Illustrative: 40-60 clusters; final size from power calculations.)

- Does a pre-heat top-up reduce income loss, debt and delayed care? What is known: PKH delivery and general economic evaluations exist, without a verified heat effect. [I4, I17] A study that could answer it: Pre-specified phased top-up trial using forecasts, with household outcomes reported only in aggregate. (Illustrative: two hot seasons across 40-60 clusters.)

- Which heat-related crop losses meet AUTP damage rules and receive timely support? What is known: Drought insurance terms and extension routes are published. [I11] A study that could answer it: Crop-season panel combining weather, field loss assessment and anonymised aggregate claim outcomes, without publishing farm locations. (Illustrative: 1,000-1,500 insured and comparable uninsured farm households.)

- [Unmeasured: On time, Adequate] Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work? What is known: Government reports count the families paid each quarter, without payment dates set against heat or amounts set against losses. A study that could answer it: Link payment dates with heat records and a short household survey on lost work and spending. (Illustrative: about 500 families in two provinces over one year)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible, Documented, Applied] Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it? What is known: An evaluation in Bandung and Medan measured enrolment: registration help raised it by 3.5 percentage points and full subsidy by 18.6, while information alone had no measured effect. Awareness, documents and applications were not measured as separate steps. A study that could answer it: Follow the same workers through awareness, documents and application, with and without help to register. (Illustrative: about 1,000 workers in two cities)

Sources: Social Security Fund: अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र सामाजिक सुरक्षा योजना https://www.ssf.gov.np/list/operating-schemes/informal-sector-scheme; International Labour Organization, 2025: Nepal launches national campaign to bring informal workers into social security https://www.ilo.org/resource/news/nepal-launches-national-campaign-bring-informal-workers-social-security

#### Where no public system responds in Nepal (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Migrant continuity: the allowance FAQ provides an administrative transfer route after a documented move; that is different from seamless access for seasonal workers away from permanent residence. (Sources: Department of National ID and Civil Registration: प्राय सोधिने प्रश्नहरु : सामाजिक सुरक्षा https://www.donidcr.gov.np/pages/mostly-asked-questions--social-security-4/)

- Agricultural heat loss: premium support was described, but current heat-loss definitions, claims timelines and tenant-farmer access were not verified. (Sources: Ministry of Finance / United Nations Development Programme, 2026: Integrated National Financing Framework Financing Strategy for Pro-Employment Economic Growth of Nepal with Action Plan https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-02/final_web_version_infs_9_feb_2026_0.pdf)

- Heat anticipatory cash: the urban protocol concerns selected places and planned households; it does not establish a standing nationwide public payment. (Sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/downloadfile/93851/sEAP2025NP02_MDRNP020)

- Debt and asset recovery after heat: no completed heat social-protection impact evaluation was read. Statistically non-significant later flood outcomes are not a heat null result. (Sources: Christian et al., 2025: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal https://bfi.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/BFI_WP_2025-140.pdf)

#### Open questions for Nepal (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- Does pre-heat cash reduce lost earnings and medical spending for outdoor-worker households? What is known: An urban heat protocol exists without a completed impact evaluation in the sources read. [N12] A study that could answer it: Randomised or pre-specified phased delivery across comparable neighbourhoods, recording timing, income, care and coping costs in aggregate. (Illustrative design: 40-60 clusters over two hot seasons; power calculation before final sampling.)

- Which step limits qualifying SSF access among informal workers? What is known: Pre-launch awareness data and later registration reports describe different periods. [N7, N8] A study that could answer it: Follow a representative cohort from information through contribution qualification and benefit receipt, with anonymised aggregate reporting. (Illustrative design: 1,500-2,000 workers across several municipalities.)

- How often does public insurance meet the full cost of heat-related care? What is known: Enrolment is measured; current heat-specific claims and complete costs are not. [N4, N5, N22] A study that could answer it: Prospective facility and household cost study with diagnosed heat cases, matched service records under consent, and published aggregate results only. (Illustrative design: 10-15 facilities across a hot season; case-volume check before sizing.)

- Does a supported transfer process reduce allowance interruption after migration? What is known: A documented allowance transfer route exists; actual seasonal continuity was not measured. [N1] A study that could answer it: Phased assistance through wards, comparing aggregate transfer completion, payment interruption and travel cost. (Illustrative design: 20-30 ward pairs over one renewal and payment cycle.)

- [Unmeasured: Adequate, On time] Do allowances arrive on time and cover what a hot season costs older people and outdoor-worker households? What is known: Awareness of the Social Security Fund, enrolment and receipt are measured in the sources checked; the adequacy and timing of allowances in hot months are not. A study that could answer it: Record payment dates and heat-season costs for allowance households in the Tarai. (Illustrative: about 400 households in four municipalities)

- [Unmeasured: Eligible, Documented, Applied] Among people who qualify for an allowance, how many hold the documents and have applied? What is known: In the sources checked, eligibility, documents and applications are not measured as separate steps. A study that could answer it: A records review with local governments that counts eligible people, documents held and applications made. (Illustrative: six wards in three municipalities)

### Singapore (research as of 6 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- KNOWN heat-specific rule: qualifying work-related heat illness can support WICA claims, and specified heat-rest breaks are considered paid work. Actual heat-claim acceptance, payment time and compensation outcomes were not verified. - INFERRED research estimate: HeatSafe values productivity loss, without establishing observed wage deductions or the effect of benefits. No causal heat social-protection outcome or heat-specific null evaluation was opened. (Sources: National University of Singapore Medicine, 2024: Heat stress causes lower fertility, productivity and reduced cognitive capacity: Project HeatSafe https://medicine.nus.edu.sg/news/heat-stress-causes-lower-fertility-productivity-and-reduced-cognitive-capacity-project-heatsafe/)

Farm grants and business credit are adaptation and cashflow routes, rather than household heat-loss insurance. (Sources: Ministry of Manpower, 2026: MOM Enhances Heat Stress Protection for Workers Amid Rising Heat Risks https://www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/2026/0828-enhancements-to-heat-stress-framework; Ministry of Manpower, 2026: Enhanced Primary Care Plan brings healthcare closer to migrant workers while lowering or maintaining costs for almost all employers https://www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/2026/0806-enhanced-primary-care-plan-appointment-of-new-aos; Enterprise Singapore, 2026: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan https://www.enterprisesg.gov.sg/financial-support/enterprise-financing-scheme---sme-working-capital; Singapore Food Agency, 2026: Agri-food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund https://www.sfa.gov.sg/recognition-programmes-grants/grants/agri-food-cluster-transformation-act-fund)

#### Schemes in Singapore

- ComCare Interim Assistance: 2026 enhancement (Disaster relief, national). Run by: Ministry of Social and Family Development. Who is eligible: Qualifying lower-income households under enhanced interim criteria. What it gives: At least S$250 monthly, up to three months, during the August-December 2026 enhancement. How it is delivered: Interim assistance route; detailed application process not fully verified. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: General temporary relief, without a verified heat trigger. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of Singapore, 2026: Managing Cost of Living in Singapore https://www.gov.sg/features/cost-of-living/

- Workfare Income Supplement (Cash, national). Run by: Central Provident Fund Board. Who is eligible: Eligible citizens aged 30+ or qualifying people with disabilities; income, property and other tests apply. What it gives: Earnings/age-dependent cash and CPF support. Employee allocation is 40% cash and 60% CPF; 2026 maximum not verified. How it is delivered: Automatic employee assessment from contribution/income records; PayNow, bank or GovCash. Documents: Employee administrative records; self-employed reporting and contributions differ. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: 2026 employee calculator: payment two months after month worked; actual delay not measured. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: supplements earnings, with possible gaps when heat reduces qualifying work; not a paid hot-day entitlement. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Central Provident Fund Board, 2026: Workfare Income Supplement https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/government-support/workfare-income-supplement; Central Provident Fund Board, 2026: Workfare Income Supplement Employee Work Year 2026 Calculator https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/workfare-income-supplement-employee-work-year-2026-calculator

- Silver Support Scheme (Pension, national). Run by: Government of Singapore / CPF administration. Who is eligible: Eligible citizens aged 65+ meeting work-history, household-income and housing tests. What it gives: S$215-S$1,080 quarterly across published bands. How it is delivered: Automatic assessment; PayNow, bank or GovCash. Documents: No application; administrative records support annual assessment. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Published quarterly advance schedule; observed payment delay not verified. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Manpower: Silver Support Scheme https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/silver-support-scheme

- CDC Vouchers Scheme: June 2026 tranche (Food, national). Run by: Government of Singapore / Community Development Councils. Who is eligible: Qualifying Singaporean households; complete claiming rules not opened. What it gives: S$500 June 2026 tranche; total-year and expiry terms not verified. How it is delivered: Voucher scheme; current detailed claim process not verified. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: spending support can ease food costs; it is not heat-loss compensation. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of Singapore, 2026: Managing Cost of Living in Singapore https://www.gov.sg/features/cost-of-living/

- GST Voucher / additional U-Save utility rebates (Cash, national). Run by: Government of Singapore. Who is eligible: Eligible HDB households under scheme conditions. What it gives: Government page lists up to S$190 additional rebates in October 2026 and January 2027; tranche details unverified. How it is delivered: Utility-bill rebate; not freely withdrawable household cash. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: bill relief can help with cooling costs, without verifying cooling equipment or sufficient electricity access. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of Singapore, 2026: Managing Cost of Living in Singapore https://www.gov.sg/features/cost-of-living/

- MediShield Life (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Health / Central Provident Fund Board. Who is eligible: Singapore citizens and permanent residents under the lifelong scheme. What it gives: Current policy-year claim maximum S$200,000; treatment limits and patient cost sharing apply. How it is delivered: Insurance payment for covered care through health-service institutions. Documents: Current treatment claim and financial-support checklist not fully verified. Partly follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: qualifying hospital treatment could cushion a heat health shock; no paid heat-claims series was read. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health, 2026: MediShield Life Benefits https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-benefits/; Ministry of Health, 2024: Managing medical bills https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/keeping-healthcare-affordable/managing-medical-bills/

- MediSave (Health care, national). Run by: Central Provident Fund Board / Ministry of Health. Who is eligible: Citizens and permanent residents with applicable account and withdrawal eligibility. What it gives: Own medical savings under withdrawal limits; not a new public cash grant. How it is delivered: Approved medical payments and insurance premiums. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: balances may help pay eligible care, while reducing savings available for later needs. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health, 2024: Managing medical bills https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/keeping-healthcare-affordable/managing-medical-bills/

- MediFund (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Health / approved institutions and MediFund Committees. Who is eligible: Subsidised citizens with difficulty paying remaining bills after other support. What it gives: Case-specific medical-bill assistance; no fixed grant. How it is delivered: Medical social workers and institutional committee assessment. Documents: Financial, health and household assessment records; full checklist varies and was not extracted. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: residual heat-related bills may qualify under assessment; actual heat approvals were not measured. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health, 2024: MediFund https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medifund/

- Community Health Assist Scheme (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Health. Who is eligible: Singapore citizens; subsidy card and service categories determine support. What it gives: CHAS Blue common-illness subsidy up to S$18.50/visit; other categories differ. How it is delivered: Participating GP and dental clinics. Documents: Applicable eligibility/card and identity records; current checklist not fully verified. Partly follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: No specific heat-diagnosis subsidy decision was verified; subsidised visits are not necessarily free. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health, 2025: Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/chas/

- Work Injury Compensation Act benefits (Insurance, national). Run by: Ministry of Manpower / employers, platform operators and insurers as applicable. Who is eligible: Covered workers with qualifying work-related injury or occupational disease. What it gives: Medical leave wages, medical expenses up to S$53,000 or one year, and applicable incapacity/death compensation. How it is delivered: Work-injury reporting, medical assessment and compensation process. Documents: Work-relatedness, medical and employment evidence; full checklist not extracted. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: KNOWN rule: heat-related work illness can support a claim; actual receipt and processing by heat diagnosis were not verified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. - Primary Care Plan for eligible migrant workers (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Manpower / contracted Anchor Operators and employers. Who is eligible: Specified Work Permit/S Pass holders in covered dormitories or CMP sectors; domestic workers excluded from this requirement. What it gives: Primary care; current co-pay S$5 for physical consultation and S$2 telemedicine. How it is delivered: Employer purchase, designated clinics, telemedicine and listed transport. Documents: Work-pass/employer enrolment and service registration; full checklist not extracted. Partly follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: acute care may help; emergency specialist/hospital bills and heat-related wage loss need separate routes. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Manpower: What is the Primary Care Plan (PCP) https://www.mom.gov.sg/primary-care-plan/what-is-pcp; Ministry of Manpower, 2026: Enhanced Primary Care Plan brings healthcare closer to migrant workers while lowering or maintaining costs for almost all employers https://www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/2026/0806-enhanced-primary-care-plan-appointment-of-new-aos; Ministry of Manpower: Getting primary care services under the Primary Care Plan (PCP) https://www.mom.gov.sg/primary-care-plan/getting-primary-care-services

- Enterprise Financing Scheme - SME Working Capital Loan (Credit, national). Run by: Enterprise Singapore / participating financial institutions. Who is eligible: Eligible Singapore-registered enterprises with local equity and SME criteria. What it gives: Up to S$500,000 per borrower over up to five years; lender sets interest. Borrower repays 100%. How it is delivered: Participating lender assessment; enterprise application system. Documents: Business, ownership and financial records; lender-specific checklist not extracted. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. - Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund (Livelihood support, national). Run by: Singapore Food Agency. Who is eligible: Eligible local farms with a valid SFA farm licence and approved project. What it gives: Technology and capability grants; component-specific rates. ACT Fund 2 is available from 2026. How it is delivered: Business Grants Portal with CorpPass and project assessment. Documents: Farm licence, proposal and component-specific records. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Around 12-20 weeks to process a complete application; disbursement time not verified. #### Where no public system responds in Singapore (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Self-employed workers' lost hot-day earnings: WIS depends on qualifying work and income; a universal paid heat work-stoppage entitlement was not verified. WICA coverage of employees and covered platform work does not establish coverage of every self-employed person. (Sources: Central Provident Fund Board, 2026: Workfare Income Supplement https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/government-support/workfare-income-supplement; Central Provident Fund Board, 2026: Workfare Income Supplement Employee Work Year 2026 Calculator https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/workfare-income-supplement-employee-work-year-2026-calculator; Ministry of Manpower, 2025: Updated coverage of reportable and compensable occupational diseases (ODs) under WSHA and WICA https://www.mom.gov.sg/workplace-safety-and-health/od-under-wsha-and-wica)

- Work-related heat illness: a claim route exists, but eligibility, medical evidence and claim acceptance stand between illness and compensation. Actual heat-specific receipt was not measured in the sources read. (Sources: Ministry of Manpower: Types of compensation under WICA https://www.mom.gov.sg/workplace-safety-and-health/work-injury-compensation/types-of-compensation; Ministry of Manpower: FAQs on Heat stress measures for outdoor work https://www.mom.gov.sg/heat-stress-measures-for-outdoor-work/faqs-on-heat-stress-measures-for-outdoor-work)

- Migrant-worker healthcare: PCP eligibility excludes migrant domestic workers from this requirement, and other migrant groups have different routes. Citizen or permanent-resident health cover is not a proxy for all migrant cover. - Cooling costs: U-Save reaches eligible households under housing and scheme rules; it is not a guarantee of cooling equipment, tolerable indoor temperatures or support for every tenancy. - Agricultural loss: ACT supports farm investment and EFS-WCL supports business cashflow. Neither opened rule is crop-loss insurance or household heat-income compensation. (Sources: Enterprise Singapore, 2026: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan https://www.enterprisesg.gov.sg/financial-support/enterprise-financing-scheme---sme-working-capital; Singapore Food Agency, 2026: Agri-food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund https://www.sfa.gov.sg/recognition-programmes-grants/grants/agri-food-cluster-transformation-act-fund)

#### Open questions for Singapore (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- How often do work-related heat illnesses move from report to accepted and paid WICA claim? What is known: Heat is recognised and benefit types are published; heat-specific process counts were not verified. [S13, S14, S15] A study that could answer it: Secure aggregate reporting of notified, filed, accepted and paid claims with time intervals and broad worker categories. (Illustrative: all available cases across several hot seasons; no individual case details published.)

- Does PCP access reduce total costs and delayed care during hot periods for covered migrant workers? What is known: A patient-experience survey exists, without a heat-specific causal comparison. [S17] A study that could answer it: Prospective hot-season facility and worker survey with pre-specified comparison periods, full care costs and aggregate results. (Illustrative: 10-15 clinics; final size based on expected heat case volume.)

- How consistently do workers receive and use paid heat-rest breaks? What is known: Official guidance recognises specified breaks as paid work; implementation outcomes were not verified. [S14] A study that could answer it: Confidential worker and employer survey plus aggregate work-schedule observations across heat levels, without individual tracking. (Illustrative: 40-60 worksites across several exposed sectors.)

- Which access steps explain non-receipt of temporary support during heat-related household income loss? What is known: National ComCare receipt counts and assisted-application routes exist. [S1, S29] A study that could answer it: Representative repeated household survey measuring awareness through on-time receipt, including explicit residency eligibility checks. (Illustrative: 1,500-2,000 households over two hot seasons.)

- [Unmeasured: Adequate, On time] Does temporary support cover the income lost when heat cuts work, and how soon does it arrive? What is known: Counts of households receiving ComCare support and of workers receiving the Workfare Income Supplement are published; adequacy and timing against heat-related income loss are not, in the sources checked. A study that could answer it: A survey of support recipients in outdoor work that compares lost earnings in hot months with the support received and when it came. (Illustrative: about 300 households)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible, Documented, Applied, Enrolled] Do migrant workers know which medical and injury protections apply to heat illness, and do they start a claim? What is known: None of the sources checked measures awareness, applications or claims started among migrant workers for heat illness. A study that could answer it: Short surveys at dormitories and worker centres, with partner organisations, followed by records of claims started. (Illustrative: about 500 workers)

### Thailand (research as of 6 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- UNCERTAIN heat-specific delivery evidence comes from a small worker-network insurance pilot. It is separate from public entitlements and has no independently verified outcome evaluation in the sources read. (Sources: HomeNet International, 2026: HomeNet Thailand Runs a Pilot Extreme Heat Insurance Project for Informal Economy Workers https://www.homenetinternational.org/homenet-thailand-runs-a-pilot-extreme-heat-insurance-project-for-informal-economy-workers/)

#### Schemes in Thailand

- Old-Age Allowance (Pension, national). Run by: Local administrative organisations under Ministry of Interior rules. Who is eligible: Eligible older Thai residents; full current income and other-pension tests not reverified. What it gives: Monthly THB600 at 60-69; 700 at 70-79; 800 at 80-89; 1,000 at 90+. How it is delivered: Not verified. Documents: Current local application checklist unverified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; actual payment timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Department of Older Persons: การรับเบี้ยผู้สูงอายุ https://dop.go.th/th/faq/view=967

- Social Security Act Section 40 (Insurance, national). Run by: Social Security Office. Who is eligible: Qualifying self-employed or informal workers under contribution conditions. What it gives: 2026 contribution options THB70/100/300 monthly; outpatient compensation THB200/visit up to three yearly. How it is delivered: SSO contribution and claim channels. Documents: Current identity, contribution and medical-certificate checklist not fully verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Sickness cash may cushion lost earnings; it is separate from UCS treatment cover, with heat-specific receipt unknown. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Labour, 2026: Over 500,000 Section 40 Insured Persons Rejoice Following Labour Minister’s Drive to Enhance Social Security Benefits Aligned with Current Economic Conditions: Outpatient Medical Compensation Increased from 50 to 200 Baht/Visit; Maximum Income Compensation for Disability Cases Raised from 1,000 to 3,000 Baht https://www.mol.go.th/en/news/over-500000-section-40-insured-persons-rejoice-following-labour-ministers-drive-to-enhance-social-security-benefits-aligned-with-current-economic-conditions-outpatient-medical-compensation-increased-from-50-to-200-baht-visit-maximum-income-compensation-for-disability-cases-raised-from-1000-to-3000-baht

- Child allowance under Sections 33 and 39 (Cash, national). Run by: Social Security Office. Who is eligible: Qualifying insured parents; at least 12 contribution months in the preceding 36 months. What it gives: THB1,000/child/month, up to three children aged birth to six. How it is delivered: SSO child-benefit process. Documents: Legal parenthood and child age need verification; full claim checklist not extracted. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; observed delay unknown. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Social Security Office, 2026: สิทธิกรณีสงเคราะห์บุตร https://www.sso.go.th/wpr/main/service/%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%87%E0%B8%97%E0%B8%B8%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%87%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%A1_detail_detail_1_125_694/234_234

- Emergency crop-disaster assistance (Disaster relief, national). Run by: Department of Agricultural Extension / provincial authorities / BAAC. Who is eligible: Previously registered growers with assessed damage in a declared assistance area. What it gives: May 2026 notice: rice THB1,340/rai; field crops/vegetables 1,980; perennial crops 4,048; up to 30 rai/household. How it is delivered: District agriculture assessment and BAAC transfer. Documents: Updated pre-disaster farmer registration and form กษ 01 with local damage certification. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Notice describes roughly 60 days after application; this is guidance, not a measured payment distribution. Why it matters in heat: Drought or heat-related crop damage depends on declaration and damage rules; universal direct heat cover is not established. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Department of Agricultural Extension, 2026: เกษตรฯ เผย 3 สิ่ง เกษตรกรควรทำ เพื่อรับการช่วยเหลือ เมื่อประสบภัยพิบัติด้านพืช https://doaenews.doae.go.th/archives/31902

- Nationwide Disaster Insurance Program (Insurance, national). Run by: Ministry of Interior / disaster-management and insurance arrangements. Who is eligible: Eligible residences under announced policy conditions. What it gives: Residential cover up to THB100,000 for listed perils; other limits apply. How it is delivered: Official damage assessment and insurance claims. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Floods, windstorms and earthquakes are listed; heat is not listed in the opened announcement. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government Public Relations Department, 2026: Launch of Nationwide Disaster Insurance Program Effective 1 October 2026 https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/547200

#### Open questions for Thailand (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- Does Section 40 sickness compensation reach informal workers diagnosed with heat illness? What is known: Current benefit changes are published; heat-specific applications and payments were not verified. [T3] A study that could answer it: Prospective claims-pathway study tracking aggregate awareness, documentation, accepted claims, value and delay. (Illustrative: several provinces over two hot seasons; final size based on case flow.)

- Does heat-triggered insurance preserve earnings and reduce debt without changing essential work hours? What is known: A worker-network pilot and partner reports exist without an independent impact estimate. [T15, T16] A study that could answer it: Pre-registered phased rollout with agreed comparison clusters, measuring income, care costs, rest and coping in aggregate. (Illustrative: 40-60 clusters across two hot seasons.)

- How different are social-insurance coverage maps based on residence and employer registration? What is known: SSO metadata describes different location concepts by section. [T11] A study that could answer it: Secure institutional aggregation of both location definitions; publish only province-level differences and uncertainty. (Illustrative: one year of all available provincial aggregate records.)

- How much heat-related crop loss is met by declared-disaster relief, and how quickly? What is known: Crop-relief rates, documents and procedure are published. [T5] A study that could answer it: Crop-season household panel and administrative aggregate audit of declarations, assessed losses, payment dates and recovery. (Illustrative: 1,000-1,500 households across several agroclimatic areas.)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible, Documented, Applied, Enrolled, Received, Adequate] For older people and informal workers, which is the first step of access where support stops in a hot season? What is known: None of the sources checked measures any step of access for the schemes on this page in Thailand. A study that could answer it: A household survey that follows the old-age allowance and Section 40 through all eight steps, for the same people. (Illustrative: about 1,000 households in three provinces)

- [Unmeasured: On time] Does crop relief after a declared disaster arrive in time to matter for the next season? What is known: None of the sources checked measures when relief reaches farmers compared with the loss. A study that could answer it: Compare declaration, claim and payment dates for crop relief across districts. (Illustrative: records from ten districts over two seasons)

## Watch Common Shade grow

https://beattheheat.asia/growing/

See what we are learning, what is changing, and how it connects to protection from extreme heat. This is a record of how the knowledge commons has changed, not a measure of protection achieved. 94 changes are recorded since 23 October 2026, 5 of them corrections or revised interpretations and 3 questions opened. "Why it matters" is Common Shade's reading; "What the source says" is quoted from the source.

### How the work behind the commons grew

Dated by the publication date of the work Common Shade draws on (1123 of 1956 works dated; 808 have no established date yet, 25 only an "online by" date; 481 links to organisations are counted apart and never dated). Common Shade began gathering this work in October 2026; the dates below are when the work was published, not when it was added.

- Before 2024: 471 works. Financing: 81; Institutions and plans: 64; Practical measures: 100; Experience: 23; Evidence: 203.

- 2024: 196 works published (94 with a known month), 667 in all by the end of the period. Financing: 118; Institutions and plans: 90; Practical measures: 135; Experience: 44; Evidence: 280.

- 2025: 210 works published (123 with a known month), 877 in all by the end of the period. Financing: 173; Institutions and plans: 118; Practical measures: 183; Experience: 69; Evidence: 334.

- 2026 so far: 246 works published (142 with a known month), 1123 in all by the end of the period. Financing: 230; Institutions and plans: 138; Practical measures: 248; Experience: 98; Evidence: 409.
